hero.title: Natural Rough Diamonds: Professional Sourcing and Trade Guide
introParagraphs: Rough natural diamonds are diamonds that have been recovered from the earth but have not yet completed the cutting and polishing process.
They are also called uncut diamonds or, less precisely, raw diamonds. Within the professional diamond trade, “rough diamond” is the standard term.

Buying rough is fundamentally different from purchasing a polished diamond. The buyer must evaluate the stone’s identity, morphology, inclusions, potential polished yield, legal trade documentation and commercial manufacturing risk before agreeing to a price.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: Natural rough diamonds are primarily traded between mining companies, manufacturers, registered diamond dealers and other eligible professional buyers.

Their value cannot be established from rough carat weight alone. A buyer must estimate what polished diamond or diamonds could be produced, how much weight may be lost during manufacturing, the cutting risk and whether the expected polished result has sufficient market demand.
Every international rough-diamond transaction must also follow the applicable Kimberley Process, customs, sanctions and dealer-registration requirements.

whoPurchases.title: Who Normally Purchases Rough Diamonds?
introParagraphs: Rough-diamond buying is generally intended for eligible professional participants such as:
bullets: Jewellery manufacturers with an established cutting partner
Mining companies and authorised tender participants
Specialist investors with professional manufacturing and compliance support
closingParagraphs: Consumers seeking a diamond for a ring will usually find a polished, independently graded natural diamond more practical. Rough weight does not indicate the size, grade or value of the finished stone.

howEvaluated.title: How Are Rough Natural Diamonds Evaluated?

subsections.title: Natural Origin Identification
introParagraphs: A rough crystal should not be accepted as natural based only on appearance.

richParagraphs.value: Natural, HPHT-grown and CVD-grown diamonds can require professional gemmological testing to distinguish them reliably. GIA notes that laboratory-grown and natural diamonds have closely related chemical, physical and optical properties and may require trained specialists and advanced instruments for separation. See the

richParagraphs.text: GIA natural versus laboratory-grown diamond research

subsections.title: Shape and Crystal Structure
paragraphs: The buyer examines the rough shape, growth form, surface condition and internal structure to determine possible cutting plans.
An attractive rough weight does not necessarily produce one large polished diamond. The manufacturer may decide that two smaller stones create a better commercial result.

subsections.title: Inclusions and Manufacturing Risk
introParagraphs: Internal features, fractures, stress, cavities and surface-reaching inclusions can affect:
closingParagraphs: A stone that appears clean from one direction may contain an inclusion that becomes significant during sawing or polishing.

subsections.title: Projected Polished Yield
paragraphs: Projected yield is the estimated polished weight recoverable from the rough.

The highest weight retention is not automatically the most valuable plan. A lighter polished diamond with stronger proportions, better clarity or a more desirable shape may be worth more than a heavier but poorly performing result.

subsections.title: Colour and Market Position
paragraphs: The buyer considers body colour, zoning and whether the expected polished result may fall within the colourless, near-colourless, fancy-colour or industrial market.
Final colour cannot always be judged safely from photographs or uncontrolled lighting.

richParagraphs.value: The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme applies specifically to international trade in rough diamonds.

The Belgian FPS Economy states that rough diamonds entering or leaving the European Union must be accompanied by a valid Kimberley Process certificate, packed in a tamper-proof container and traded only between Kimberley Process participants. Belgian rough-diamond exports also require evidence showing how the exporter obtained the goods. Review the current

A Kimberley Process certificate should not be presented as proof of every possible ethical, labour, environmental or human-rights claim. Belgian Foreign Affairs has acknowledged that the scheme’s conflict-diamond definition has limitations. Additional supplier due diligence and provenance evidence may therefore be necessary. enquiryProcess.title: Professional Rough-Diamond Enquiry Process
introParagraphs: A properly controlled enquiry should follow these stages:

steps.title: Submit the Requirement
paragraphs: Provide the preferred size, quantity, crystal type, quality, colour, budget, manufacturing objective and destination.

steps.title: Confirm Eligibility
paragraphs: The parties should confirm dealer-registration, KYC, AML, sanctions and destination requirements before discussing shipment.

steps.title: Review Availability and Documents
paragraphs: The seller should identify the parcel, ownership evidence, weight, quantity, origin documentation and applicable Kimberley Process records.

steps.title: Complete Specialist Evaluation
paragraphs: The rough should be examined by someone qualified to assess identity, manufacturing risk and projected polished yield.

steps.title: Issue a Written Quotation
paragraphs: The quotation should state the exact goods, assumptions, currency, validity period, payment terms, inspection conditions and delivery responsibilities.

steps.title: Complete Export and Import Controls
paragraphs: The shipment must follow all relevant Kimberley Process, customs, sanctions, insurance and tamper-resistant packaging requirements.

items.question: What is a natural rough diamond?
items.answer: A natural rough diamond is a diamond formed through geological processes that has not yet completed cutting and polishing.

items.question: Are rough and raw diamonds the same?
items.answer: “Raw diamond” is an informal description. “Rough diamond” is the standard trade and regulatory term.

items.question: Can anyone buy rough diamonds?
items.answer: Eligibility depends on the jurisdiction and transaction. International rough-diamond trade is normally conducted between authorised professional participants and is subject to compliance controls.

items.question: Do rough diamonds have GIA grading reports?
items.answer: Standard GIA natural-diamond grading reports are intended for loose polished diamonds. GIA’s rough analysis is primarily connected to its Diamond Origin programme and does not function like a normal polished grading report.

items.question: How can I confirm that a rough diamond is natural?
items.answer: Appearance alone is insufficient. Reliable separation from laboratory-grown material may require professional gemmological examination and advanced testing.

items.question: How is a rough diamond valued?
items.answer: Value depends on identity, weight, shape, colour, inclusions, projected polished yield, cutting risk, manufacturing cost, documentation and demand for the expected polished result.

items.question: Does a Kimberley Process certificate prove the mining country?
items.answer: The certificate records information required for the shipment, but complete mine-level provenance may require additional evidence. Review the original certificate, invoice and supporting chain-of-custody documents.

items.question: Does Kimberley Process compliance prove that a diamond is ethically sourced?
items.answer: It addresses conflict diamonds under the scheme’s defined scope. It does not automatically prove every labour, environmental, human-rights or sustainability claim.

items.question: Can I value a rough diamond from photographs?
items.answer: Photographs may support an initial discussion but cannot reliably establish identity, internal condition, manufacturing risk or polished yield.

items.question: Can Dalila Diamonds source natural rough diamonds?
items.answer: This must be confirmed directly for the requested parcel, buyer, destination and transaction. Dalila should not be represented as a rough-diamond supplier until its service scope and regulatory eligibility are documented.
